## Renaming meetings: both the CLI and the MCP tool are broken (added 2026-08-29)

Two independent failures, and the second one lies about succeeding.

**1. `fireflies-pp-cli transcripts update` always fails.** It sends the id as a bare
mutation argument; the API wants it wrapped in an input object:

```
CLI sends: updateMeetingTitle(id: ..., title: ...)
API wants: updateMeetingTitle(input: {id: ..., title: ...})
```

Result is `HTTP 400 ... Unknown argument "id" on field "Mutation.updateMeetingTitle"`.
Note the field really is `id`, **not** `meetingId` — a direct call with `meetingId`
returns `Field "UpdateMeetingTitleInput.id" of required type "String!" was not provided`.
Don't "fix" the CLI by renaming the field; the shape is what's wrong.

**2. The Fireflies MCP tool `fireflies_update_meeting_title` is unreliable and its
`success:true` means nothing.** Writes are *erratically delayed*, not simply dropped:
on 2026-08-29 only 2 of 7 renames persisted promptly, 5 returned success and had not
landed after 8 minutes of polling, and one diagnostic write ("… v2") surfaced roughly
20–30 minutes later. So a "failed" MCP rename can still land an hour on and clobber a
good title. **This looked exactly like a rate limit and is not one** —
`name-meetings/REFERENCE.md` documents a "hard daily rate limit", which sent the
diagnosis down a 45-minute dead end. Never use MCP for renames; never send a throwaway
"test" title through it, because late arrival makes the probe destructive.

**Working path — call GraphQL directly with the keychain API key:**

```python
q = "mutation($input: UpdateMeetingTitleInput!){ updateMeetingTitle(input:$input){ title } }"
# POST https://api.fireflies.ai/graphql, Authorization: Bearer <FIREFLIES_API_KEY>
# variables: {"input": {"id": <meetingId>, "title": <newTitle>}}
```

All 7 renames applied first try this way, verified by read-back. Reusable script:
`~/.claude/jobs/*/tmp/rename_direct.py` (regenerate it; job dirs are cleaned up).

**Verification traps:**
- `transcripts get <id> --data-source live --no-cache` is trustworthy and is the
  read-back to use. `--no-cache` matters.
- The **list** endpoint (what `sync` + `transcripts find` read) lags the single-transcript
  endpoint by minutes. A fresh rename can be correct live and stale in `find` after a
  `sync --full`. Wait ~4 min and re-sync before exporting, or the vault filename bakes in
  the old title.
- Never verify a rename by exit code or by the mutation's own response.

**Backgrounded polling scripts appear to produce no output** until they exit — the file
stays 0 bytes mid-run. Don't conclude the script died; read it again after it completes.

Related: [[fireflies-cli-broken-on-mac]]

---

## `transcripts find --json` returns a bare LIST (added 2026-09-02)

`fireflies-pp-cli transcripts find --json --agent` emits a **top-level JSON array**, not an
envelope object. A parser written as `d.get("data") or d.get("items") or d` dies with
`AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`. Guard with
`items = d if isinstance(d, list) else d.get("data", [])`.

**The rename → export loop works end to end** (verified 2026-09-02, 3 meetings):
`scripts/rename.py <id> "<title>"` → `sleep 270` → `sync --full --resources transcripts`
→ `find` shows new titles → `meeting-sync/scripts/sync.py --no-sync` exports with the
good slug. The 4-minute wait is mandatory; skipping it bakes the stale title into the
vault filename. Run the sleep as a **background** Bash job — the foreground tool caps at 120s.

**Vault header placement:** `assets/meeting-header.md` goes after the metadata block's
`---` rule (line 9 of the export), *before* `## Summary` — not at line 1. Exported files
have no YAML frontmatter, so "after frontmatter" reads as line 1 and would be wrong;
match the 237 existing files instead.

**Open to-do (moved out of Tier B working memory 2026-09-09): rotate the Fireflies API
key.** Rotate it in the Fireflies dashboard, then update the stored secret — secrets on
this machine live in the macOS Keychain, never in `~/.zshrc`.

241	**Resolved 2026-08-11.** Recording the trap because the error message points the wrong way.
242	
243	`fireflies-pp-cli` failed on **every** command and every `--data-source` (including
244	`live`) with:
245	
246	```
247	Error: querying: unable to open database file: out of memory (14)
248	```
249	
250	"Out of memory" is wrong — SQLite 14 is `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`. The real cause: the local
251	mirror had **never been created on this Mac**. Two things were missing after the
252	Windows → Mac migration:
253	
254	1. No `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` anywhere — not env, not disk, not Keychain.
255	2. No database. `sync` had never been run here.
256	
257	**`--data-source live` does not bypass the database.** Read commands open it regardless,
258	so "live" fails identically until a sync exists. That is what makes the error so
259	misleading — it looks like a corrupt/locked DB rather than a missing one.
260	
261	**Fix:** the key is in the login Keychain as of 2026-08-13, not plaintext in
262	`~/.zshrc`. `~/.zshrc` exports it by *reading* the Keychain:
263	`export FIREFLIES_API_KEY="$(security find-generic-password -s FIREFLIES_API_KEY -a "$USER" -w)"`.
264	Then `fireflies-pp-cli sync`. See [[path-shadowing-and-cleanup]].
265	Synced 189 transcripts / 200 records on first run.
266	
267	**The DB lives at `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db`** (XDG data dir), *not*
268	`~/.fireflies-pp-cli/` — that directory exists but stays empty and is a red herring.
269	
270	**Shell gotcha:** `~/.zshrc` exports are invisible to Claude Code's Bash tool (it runs
271	non-interactive bash and does not source zshrc). Load them explicitly per command:
272	`eval "$(grep -m1 '^[[:space:]]*export[[:space:]]\+VARNAME' ~/.zshrc)"`
273	
274	**Knock-on effect worth remembering:** `meeting-sync` hard-stops on auth failure and
275	`weekly-review` calls it first, so this single missing credential silently disabled both
276	rituals. The vault meeting corpus froze at 2026-08-03 and `Inbox/weekly-review/` went
277	empty after 2026-07-31. A lapse that reads as a discipline problem was a missing env var.
278	Design rule: recurring skills must **degrade and report staleness**, never hard-stop.

313	## Renaming meetings: both the CLI and the MCP tool are broken (added 2026-08-29)
314	
315	Two independent failures, and the second one lies about succeeding.
316	
317	**1. `fireflies-pp-cli transcripts update` always fails.** It sends the id as a bare
318	mutation argument; the API wants it wrapped in an input object:
319	
320	```
321	CLI sends: updateMeetingTitle(id: ..., title: ...)
322	API wants: updateMeetingTitle(input: {id: ..., title: ...})
323	```
324	
325	Result is `HTTP 400 ... Unknown argument "id" on field "Mutation.updateMeetingTitle"`.
326	Note the field really is `id`, **not** `meetingId` — a direct call with `meetingId`
327	returns `Field "UpdateMeetingTitleInput.id" of required type "String!" was not provided`.
328	Don't "fix" the CLI by renaming the field; the shape is what's wrong.
329	
330	**2. The Fireflies MCP tool `fireflies_update_meeting_title` is unreliable and its
331	`success:true` means nothing.** Writes are *erratically delayed*, not simply dropped:
332	on 2026-08-29 only 2 of 7 renames persisted promptly, 5 returned success and had not
333	landed after 8 minutes of polling, and one diagnostic write ("… v2") surfaced roughly
334	20–30 minutes later. So a "failed" MCP rename can still land an hour on and clobber a
335	good title. **This looked exactly like a rate limit and is not one** —
336	`name-meetings/REFERENCE.md` documents a "hard daily rate limit", which sent the
337	diagnosis down a 45-minute dead end. Never use MCP for renames; never send a throwaway
338	"test" title through it, because late arrival makes the probe destructive.
339	
340	**Working path — call GraphQL directly with the keychain API key:**
341	
342	```python
343	q = "mutation($input: UpdateMeetingTitleInput!){ updateMeetingTitle(input:$input){ title } }"
344	# POST https://api.fireflies.ai/graphql, Authorization: Bearer <FIREFLIES_API_KEY>
345	# variables: {"input": {"id": <meetingId>, "title": <newTitle>}}
346	```
347	
348	All 7 renames applied first try this way, verified by read-back. Reusable script:
349	`~/.claude/jobs/*/tmp/rename_direct.py` (regenerate it; job dirs are cleaned up).
350	
351	**Verification traps:**
352	- `transcripts get <id> --data-source live --no-cache` is trustworthy and is the
353	  read-back to use. `--no-cache` matters.
354	- The **list** endpoint (what `sync` + `transcripts find` read) lags the single-transcript
355	  endpoint by minutes. A fresh rename can be correct live and stale in `find` after a
356	  `sync --full`. Wait ~4 min and re-sync before exporting, or the vault filename bakes in
357	  the old title.
358	- Never verify a rename by exit code or by the mutation's own response.
359	
360	**Backgrounded polling scripts appear to produce no output** until they exit — the file
361	stays 0 bytes mid-run. Don't conclude the script died; read it again after it completes.
362	
363	Related: [[fireflies-cli-broken-on-mac]]

367	## `transcripts find --json` returns a bare LIST (added 2026-09-02)
368	
369	`fireflies-pp-cli transcripts find --json --agent` emits a **top-level JSON array**, not an
370	envelope object. A parser written as `d.get("data") or d.get("items") or d` dies with
371	`AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`. Guard with
372	`items = d if isinstance(d, list) else d.get("data", [])`.
373	
374	**The rename → export loop works end to end** (verified 2026-09-02, 3 meetings):
375	`scripts/rename.py <id> "<title>"` → `sleep 270` → `sync --full --resources transcripts`
376	→ `find` shows new titles → `meeting-sync/scripts/sync.py --no-sync` exports with the
377	good slug. The 4-minute wait is mandatory; skipping it bakes the stale title into the
378	vault filename. Run the sleep as a **background** Bash job — the foreground tool caps at 120s.
379	
380	**Vault header placement:** `assets/meeting-header.md` goes after the metadata block's
381	`---` rule (line 9 of the export), *before* `## Summary` — not at line 1. Exported files

Everything is global. That is the anti-pattern, not the achievement.

## The rule that fixes it — promotion

**Everything stays project-level until it earns global.** A skill lives in
`<project>/.claude/skills/` until it proves itself across 2+ projects, then it
gets promoted to `~/.claude/skills/`. Keeps the global load small and the blast
radius tight — so when something underperforms you can tell a *model* problem
from a *harness* problem from an *organisation* problem.

## The audit question

Not "how often did I run this skill?" but **"would the model do this fine without
the skill now?"** A skill is a crutch; as the brain gets smarter the crutch starts
to *limit* it. Seasonal skills (`forecast-capture`) and occasional ones
(`ingest-book`) are low-count by design — low usage alone is not a delete signal.

## Re-measure (BUILTIN filter is the whole trick)

Without the `BUILTIN` set you also count `/exit`, `/clear`, `/compact` and friends,
which inflates the total to 74 and buries the real skills.

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import glob,re,collections
BUILTIN={'exit','clear','compact','rename','color','login','logout','plugin','doctor',
'help','model','config','resume','cost','status','init','agents','mcp','hooks','memory',
'review','vim','terminal-setup','install-github-app','add-dir','bug','release-notes',
'pr-comments','ide','permissions','statusline','output-style','todos','export',
'privacy-settings','upgrade','fast','artifacts','tasks','loop','context','usage','rewind',
'sandbox','feedback','worktrees','skills','reload-skills','reload-plugins','bashes',
'keybindings','theme'}
c=collections.Counter()
for f in glob.glob('/Users/kristinarash/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl',recursive=True):
    try:
        for line in open(f,encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore'):
            if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line: continue
            for m in re.finditer(r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line):
                c[m.group(1)]+=1
            for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line):
                c[m.group(1)]+=1
    except Exception: pass
real={k:v for k,v in c.items() if k.split(':')[-1] not in BUILTIN and k not in BUILTIN}
print("distinct real skills ever invoked:",len(real))
print("used >=3 times:",len([k for k,v in real.items() if v>=3]))
print("used exactly once:",len([k for k,v in real.items() if v==1]))
for k,v in sorted(real.items(),key=lambda x:-x[1]): print(f"{v:5d}  {k}")
EOF
```

## Decision, 2026-09-12

**Do the skill audit BEFORE adopting Pi** (`pi.dev`) as an alternative harness.
Rationale: the leverage is the bloat, not the harness. Auditing first means any
future harness move ports ~30 good skills instead of ~200 mixed ones.

Pi facts, verified from `pi.dev/docs/latest` 2026-09-12 — full note at
`~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-pi-harness-research.md`:

1. **No sandbox, no approval flows.** "Pi does not include a built-in sandbox."
   Project trust only guards resource *loading*, not what the agent then does.
   Never run Pi in `~/DEV` or near `DexaProject`. Trial it in `~/pi-trial` or a
   container (`sbx` keeps the credential off the container).
2. **Skills port for one line.** Pi implements the Agent Skills standard and already
   auto-discovers `~/.agents/skills/` — where 45 of the skills live. Add the rest with
   `{"skills": ["~/.claude/skills"]}` in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`. It loads
   `AGENTS.md` **or** `CLAUDE.md` directly.
3. **Hooks → TypeScript extensions is a bounded port, not a rewrite** (earlier note
   said "weeks", that was wrong). Hooks here are already `.ts`; Pi's `tool_call` event
   returns `{block, reason}` — the same shape as the dcg guard.
4. **Claude subscription through Pi bills per token as "extra usage", NOT against plan
   limits.** Changes the economics of brain-swapping.

Config lives in `~/.pi/agent/` and survives npm uninstall.
See also [[hook-two-copies-trap]] and [[dcg-guard-blocks]].

## Audit outcome, 2026-09-12

**Both tiers executed.** 99 skills archived, global **160 → 61**, roster cost
**19,158 → 6,428 tokens/session (a 66% cut)**. Zero regressions: none of the 99
had ever been invoked in 414 sessions.

Decision 2026-09-12: keep the `mattpocock-skills` and `superpowers` **plugins** and
archive the local bare-name duplicates. The plugin (v1.2.3, 35 skills) ships every
duplicate removed and is newer than the July symlinks. Rule that follows: when a
plugin and a local skill share a name, **the plugin wins** — delete the local copy.

Script: `~/.claude/skills-audit-2026-09-12.sh` (archives, never deletes — undo with
`mv ~/.claude/skills-archive/2026-09-12/* ~/.claude/skills/`).
Report: `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-skill-audit.md`.

Traps found while doing it:
1. **CORRECTED 2026-09-12 — `~/.claude/skills/` IS version-controlled.** It is its own
   git repo, remote `https://github.com/erash11/claude-skills.git`, and the audit was
   committed as `3ab4467 chore: apply global skill audit` and pushed. The earlier note
   that it is "gitignored, archive is the only undo" was true only of the *`dotclaude`*
   repo, which ignores this path — a different thing. **Git IS the safety net here, and
   it is also how the cut reaches Windows.** Undo with
   `git -C ~/.claude/skills revert <sha> && git push`, not the archive folder
   (`skills-archive/` is not in the repo and never reaches the other machine).
2. **A cut in `~/.claude/skills/` does NOT reach `~/.agents/skills/`.** After the audit,
   98 of the 99 archived skills were still live in the pool (306 entries there vs 61
   canonical). Claude Code stopped seeing them; **Pi auto-discovers that folder**, so
   installing Pi would have re-exposed all of them. Always cut both.
3. **Skills live in three places and it is easy to edit the wrong copy.**
   `~/.claude/skills/` (19 entries were symlinks pointing *out* to the pool),
   `~/.agents/skills/` (Pi, Cowork), `~/.codex/skills/` (Codex, 27 symlinks + 5 real
   dirs). Count with `find -L`; plain `find` undercounts.
4. **`sync-to-codex.sh` did `rm -rf "$dst/$s"; cp -R "$SRC/$s"`** over a 7-name
   allowlist. If `$SRC/$s` ever became a symlink into `$dst`, that deletes the real
   data. `dev-sync` tells you to run it after every pull. A `.ps1` twin has the same
   shape — patch both.
5. **`~/.claude/skills/_shared/`** holds `config.json` + `Inference/` and is resolved by
   10+ skills via `parents[2]/_shared/config.json`. It has **no SKILL.md**. Never treat
   "no SKILL.md" as "orphan, delete".
6. **"606 plugin skills" is cache, not load.** Only 6 of 24 plugins are enabled
   (~37 skills exposed). The rest are disabled plugins and old cached versions.

## Executed 2026-09-12 — traps the live run found

- **Views are live links now.** `~/.agents/skills/<owned>` and `~/.codex/skills/<owned>`
  point into canonical, so anything that writes a view path writes canonical
  (`graphify install --platform agents` does; see [[graphify-runtime-setup]]).
- **`skillOverrides` in `~/.claude/settings.json` breaks parity silently.** Codex and Pi
  ignore that file, so an owned skill set `"off"` there is hidden in Claude Code but live
  elsewhere. Perfect frontmatter does not help; `skill-portability-check.py` fails it.
  Resolved 2026-09-13: Eric re-enabled the 7 (ArXiv, ISA, Science, capture-insight,
  library-review, pp-espn, session-miner) — `~/.claude` commit `21c686d`, checker 42/42.
  Never set an owned skill "off" again; retire it from canonical instead.
- **Git's spelling wins, not the Mac's.** APFS is case-insensitive: the folder showed
  `Harvest` while git recorded `harvest/`. Check `git ls-files` before "fixing" a
  name to match the disk.
- **A `closeout` in another session commits your uncommitted work** (it swept Task 5's
  34 SKILL.md edits into its own commit). Commit each verified step immediately.
- **Description budget:** keep each description under ~650 chars; Claude Code caps the
  combined listing.

## Architecture decided 2026-09-12 (executed through Task 5 the same day)

**Canonical = `~/.claude/skills/`** (the git repo, real directories only, **never commit
a symlink** — Windows pulls this repo). `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.codex/skills/` are
**generated views**, rebuilt by `sync-to-codex.sh` from a complete manifest of every
canonical dir holding a SKILL.md, recorded in a `.generated-by-sync-to-codex` ownership
file so an audit can tell a generated entry from a third-party `npx skills add` install.
Symlink on Mac, copy on Windows.

Portable frontmatter contract (fires in Claude Code *and* Codex): `name` must equal the
directory name (TitleCase is legal), and `description` needs **both** a positive
"Use when …" clause with literal trigger phrases *and* a negative "Do not use …" clause.
Codex reads only `name` + `description` (+ optional `metadata.short-description`) and
ignores `argument-hint` / `allowed-tools`. Codex over-fires without the negative clause;
Claude will not trigger without the literal phrases.

Plan (Codex-approved after 6 review rounds, 10→0 findings):
`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-harness-agnostic-aios.md`.
See [[dev-layout-and-discovery]], [[hook-two-copies-trap]], [[vendored-skill-install]].

## claude.ai-synced duplicates, 2026-10-02 (doctor-plus)

`~/.claude/skills/synced/<account-id>/` is claude.ai account skills synced down (gitignored,
re-synced each start — deleting the folder does not stick). They list as `anthropic-skills:<name>`.
Where one duplicates a local skill, **local wins**: set `"anthropic-skills:<name>": "off"` in
`skillOverrides` (namespaced keys work — verified with a headless on/off control run). Done for
closeout, dev-sync, five-slides-generator, new-project, watch, last30days (2026-10-06; the
plugins `watch@claude-video` and `last30days@last30days-skill` keep them; local `watch` was
already "off"), articulation-skill (the last one re-tracked
in canonical 2026-10-02 after a 9/10 removal left untracked per-machine copies). Do not delete them on claude.ai: the synced
five-slides is written for the claude.ai sandbox and is the right copy there. The "never off" rule
above is for *owned* skills only.

## Listing trim, 2026-09-14 (doctor-plus)

**40 owned skills are `"name-only"` in `~/.claude/settings.json` `skillOverrides`**
(dotclaude commit `172d547`). 13 stay full: the ones Claude invoked itself 2+ times
(memory-write, CreateSkill, impeccable, claude-stack-doctor, codex-review, name-meetings,
project, graphify, fireflies-intake, html-to-pdf, meeting-prep, status-report) plus
sports-science-research-grounding. Chosen from the usage scan above (model calls vs typed).

- Why `name-only`, not `"off"` or `disable-model-invocation`: the name stays listed, so
  Skill-tool chains (`startup`→`dev-sync`, `weekly-review`→`meeting-sync`) still work,
  the portability checker only fails `"off"`, and Codex/Pi still see full descriptions.
- Cost: those 40 fire less on phrases ("goodnight", "capture this"). Type `/name`.
- Next-session check: if ~17 local skills still show as bare names, the listing budget
  is being eaten by plugin skills, not these. Promote a skill back to `"on"` by deleting
  its line.

## Plugin/skill dedupe, 2026-10-07

- `mattpocock-skills` now comes from Matt's own marketplace (`@mattpocock`, 1.3.1, autoUpdate).
  The `@claude-plugins-official` copy was uninstalled: that marketplace pins a commit SHA and
  lagged at 1.2.3. Prefer the author's own marketplace.
- Removed 6 untracked symlinks in `~/.claude/skills/` that shadowed plugin skills (code-review,
  grilling, handoff, prototype, teach, watch). Targets stay in `~/.agents/skills/` for Codex/Pi.
- Review skills trimmed (Eric's choice, same day): keep `mattpocock-skills:code-review` +
  `codex-review`. Built-in `code-review` set "off" (bare key; does not hit the namespaced plugin
  skill). `superpowers:requesting-code-review` "off" (Eric's call; superpowers
  executing-plans and subagent-driven-development call it by name, so their review step may fail).
- `superpowers:test-driven-development` "off" too; `mattpocock-skills:tdd` is the TDD skill.
- A description/body similarity scan of 148 active skills found no other duplicates.
=== project_fireflies-cli-broken-on-mac.md
---
name: fireflies-cli-broken-on-mac
description: "fireflies-pp-cli's misleading \"out of memory (14)\" error means the local DB was never synced — not a real failure"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 412a89e3-b64f-44e6-9c87-4766d44e6c7a
  modified: 2026-08-29T13:01:27.698Z
---

**Resolved 2026-08-11.** Recording the trap because the error message points the wrong way.

`fireflies-pp-cli` failed on **every** command and every `--data-source` (including
`live`) with:

```
Error: querying: unable to open database file: out of memory (14)
```

"Out of memory" is wrong — SQLite 14 is `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`. The real cause: the local
mirror had **never been created on this Mac**. Two things were missing after the
Windows → Mac migration:

1. No `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` anywhere — not env, not disk, not Keychain.
2. No database. `sync` had never been run here.

**`--data-source live` does not bypass the database.** Read commands open it regardless,
so "live" fails identically until a sync exists. That is what makes the error so
misleading — it looks like a corrupt/locked DB rather than a missing one.

**Fix:** the key is in the login Keychain as of 2026-08-13, not plaintext in
`~/.zshrc`. `~/.zshrc` exports it by *reading* the Keychain:
`export FIREFLIES_API_KEY="$(security find-generic-password -s FIREFLIES_API_KEY -a "$USER" -w)"`.
Then `fireflies-pp-cli sync`. See [[path-shadowing-and-cleanup]].
Synced 189 transcripts / 200 records on first run.

**The DB lives at `~/.local/share/fireflies-pp-cli/data.db`** (XDG data dir), *not*
`~/.fireflies-pp-cli/` — that directory exists but stays empty and is a red herring.

**Shell gotcha:** `~/.zshrc` exports are invisible to Claude Code's Bash tool (it runs
non-interactive bash and does not source zshrc). Load them explicitly per command:
`eval "$(grep -m1 '^[[:space:]]*export[[:space:]]\+VARNAME' ~/.zshrc)"`

**Knock-on effect worth remembering:** `meeting-sync` hard-stops on auth failure and
`weekly-review` calls it first, so this single missing credential silently disabled both
rituals. The vault meeting corpus froze at 2026-08-03 and `Inbox/weekly-review/` went
empty after 2026-07-31. A lapse that reads as a discipline problem was a missing env var.
Design rule: recurring skills must **degrade and report staleness**, never hard-stop.

---

## Transcript text requires `--live` (added 2026-08-13)

`transcripts get <id>` returns metadata, speakers, and the AI summary but **no
`sentences` array** — and neither does the local DB (`json_extract(data,'$.sentences')`
is null) nor `transcripts export`, which emits only the summary (~2.6 KB).

To get the actual dialogue, add `--live`:

```
fireflies-pp-cli transcripts get <id> --live --json
```

That returned 476 sentences / 284 KB for a 39-minute meeting, vs 6 KB without it. So
`sync` does **not** mirror transcript bodies — only metadata and summaries. Plan any
transcript-reading work around one `--live` call, then condense locally (group
consecutive sentences by `speaker_name` into turns; 476 sentences collapsed to 74 turns
/ 37 KB, which is readable in one pass).

Also: **speaker names in the AI summary can be wrong.** In the 8/13 meeting the summary
named "Aaron" and "Carrie"; the actual `speakers` array had **Erin Boyette**, and Carrie
never spoke. Trust `speakers` / `sentences`, not `summary.action_items`.

**Correction to the shell gotcha above:** as of 2026-08-13 `FIREFLIES_API_KEY` *is*
visible to the Bash tool — `doctor` reported `auth_source: env:FIREFLIES_API_KEY` with
no manual sourcing. Verify before working around it.

Related: [[status-report-sourcing]], [[gws-forms-api]]


---

## Renaming meetings: both the CLI and the MCP tool are broken (added 2026-08-29)

Two independent failures, and the second one lies about succeeding.

**1. `fireflies-pp-cli transcripts update` always fails.** It sends the id as a bare
mutation argument; the API wants it wrapped in an input object:

```
CLI sends: updateMeetingTitle(id: ..., title: ...)
API wants: updateMeetingTitle(input: {id: ..., title: ...})
```

Result is `HTTP 400 ... Unknown argument "id" on field "Mutation.updateMeetingTitle"`.
Note the field really is `id`, **not** `meetingId` — a direct call with `meetingId`
returns `Field "UpdateMeetingTitleInput.id" of required type "String!" was not provided`.
Don't "fix" the CLI by renaming the field; the shape is what's wrong.

**2. The Fireflies MCP tool `fireflies_update_meeting_title` is unreliable and its
`success:true` means nothing.** Writes are *erratically delayed*, not simply dropped:
on 2026-08-29 only 2 of 7 renames persisted promptly, 5 returned success and had not
landed after 8 minutes of polling, and one diagnostic write ("… v2") surfaced roughly
20–30 minutes later. So a "failed" MCP rename can still land an hour on and clobber a
good title. **This looked exactly like a rate limit and is not one** —
`name-meetings/REFERENCE.md` documents a "hard daily rate limit", which sent the
diagnosis down a 45-minute dead end. Never use MCP for renames; never send a throwaway
"test" title through it, because late arrival makes the probe destructive.

**Working path — call GraphQL directly with the keychain API key:**

```python
q = "mutation($input: UpdateMeetingTitleInput!){ updateMeetingTitle(input:$input){ title } }"
# POST https://api.fireflies.ai/graphql, Authorization: Bearer <FIREFLIES_API_KEY>
# variables: {"input": {"id": <meetingId>, "title": <newTitle>}}
```

All 7 renames applied first try this way, verified by read-back. Reusable script:
`~/.claude/jobs/*/tmp/rename_direct.py` (regenerate it; job dirs are cleaned up).

**Verification traps:**
- `transcripts get <id> --data-source live --no-cache` is trustworthy and is the
  read-back to use. `--no-cache` matters.
- The **list** endpoint (what `sync` + `transcripts find` read) lags the single-transcript
  endpoint by minutes. A fresh rename can be correct live and stale in `find` after a
  `sync --full`. Wait ~4 min and re-sync before exporting, or the vault filename bakes in
  the old title.
- Never verify a rename by exit code or by the mutation's own response.

**Backgrounded polling scripts appear to produce no output** until they exit — the file
stays 0 bytes mid-run. Don't conclude the script died; read it again after it completes.

Related: [[fireflies-cli-broken-on-mac]]

---

## `transcripts find --json` returns a bare LIST (added 2026-09-02)

`fireflies-pp-cli transcripts find --json --agent` emits a **top-level JSON array**, not an
envelope object. A parser written as `d.get("data") or d.get("items") or d` dies with
`AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`. Guard with
`items = d if isinstance(d, list) else d.get("data", [])`.

**The rename → export loop works end to end** (verified 2026-09-02, 3 meetings):
`scripts/rename.py <id> "<title>"` → `sleep 270` → `sync --full --resources transcripts`
→ `find` shows new titles → `meeting-sync/scripts/sync.py --no-sync` exports with the
good slug. The 4-minute wait is mandatory; skipping it bakes the stale title into the
vault filename. Run the sleep as a **background** Bash job — the foreground tool caps at 120s.

**Vault header placement:** `assets/meeting-header.md` goes after the metadata block's
`---` rule (line 9 of the export), *before* `## Summary` — not at line 1. Exported files
have no YAML frontmatter, so "after frontmatter" reads as line 1 and would be wrong;
match the 237 existing files instead.

**Open to-do (moved out of Tier B working memory 2026-09-09): rotate the Fireflies API
key.** Rotate it in the Fireflies dashboard, then update the stored secret — secrets on
this machine live in the macOS Keychain, never in `~/.zshrc`.

Built 2026-09-07. `interview-me` opens with **Part 0 — supervisor log**: three factual
questions (equipment/installs, who you talked to + sport, waiting-on/risks), 90 seconds,
asked *before* the four reflection questions. Output → `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/status-log/YYYY-MM-DD.md`
(config key `vault_status_log`). Nothing to report writes **no file**.

`status-report` reads that folder first (Step 2b item 1b), skips standing interview
questions the logs already answered, and prints "N of D days logged" in Step 8.

**Why:** roughly two thirds of what belongs in the supervisor email — equipment arriving,
installs, hallway conversations, follow-ups awaiting a reply — appears in **no** automated
source. `portfolio.json` and `_ledger.md` track building work; the report describes
departmental operations. A draft from automated sources alone is about one-third finished.

**How to apply:** Part 0 goes first and that ordering is the design, not a preference —
reflection is expensive when tired and this ritual already lapsed 49 days once. The
"N of D" count is the nudge; never backfill missing days to make it look better. Never
pad the log — `status-report` copies entries into an email to supervisors with light
editing, so an invented install becomes a false claim in front of Chris Ruf.

Traps the 09-07 cycle exposed:
- Meeting **action items are assignments, not outcomes.** Three lines nearly shipped as
  done that were only to-dos. Same failure class as `portfolio.json` `stage: shipped`.
- Writing in ASD-STE/plain-English mode **strips Eric's contractions** and the email stops
  sounding like him. Contract everything; the sent 08-24 reference is the voice test.
- `fireflies-pp-cli action-items list` exits 0 and returns empty `{}` objects — reads as
  "no open commitments" if trusted. Use the digest's inline action items.
